title: The integral inverse-image/pullback comparison respects composition
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be isomorphisms of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse images $h^{-1},k^{-1},(kh)^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. On each of $Z,W,V$ use the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,-}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_-$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the category $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For an isomorphism $g\in\{h,k,kh\}$ let $g^{-1}$ act on complexes with the module structure transported through the structure isomorphism $c_{\mathcal O_E}$, let $Lg^*$ be the completed integral pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let $\kappa^g_K:g^{-1}K\to Lg^*K$ be the specified comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b). Let $d_{h,k,K}:h^{-1}k^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}(kh)^{-1}K$ be the canonical isomorphism of inverse images, applied termwise; it is linear for the transported module structures. Let $c^E_{h,k,K}:L(kh)^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lk^*K$ be the specified integral pullback-composition isomorphism of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Then for every $N\in D^b_c(V,\mathcal O_E)$ the object $Lk^*N$ lies in $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$, and
$$c^E_{h,k,N}\circ\kappa^{kh}_N\circ d_{h,k,N}=\kappa^h_{Lk^*N}\circ h^{-1}(\kappa^k_N):h^{-1}k^{-1}N\longrightarrow Lh^*Lk^*N$$
as morphisms of $D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$. This is an equality of the specified derived morphisms, not merely of their reductions modulo $\varpi_E^n$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], integral pullback preserves $D^b_c$, so $M=Lk^*N$ is an allowed input to $\kappa^h$. The coefficient identity of [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition] gives compatibility at every $A_{E,m}$. Projecting to every quotient in the structure-map formula of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] gives the completed coefficient identity. Thus the canonical inverse-image compositor $d$ respects the transported module actions, and its termwise map descends to the derived categories.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: compatibility with composition of the integral identifications

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-integral-composition-counit-images], with its one chosen $q:P\to N$, $Q=h^{-1}k^{-1}(q)$, and $\eta:Lh^*M\xrightarrow\sim R\lim D_\bullet$. It computes the two entire-tower counit images of $a=\eta c^E\kappa^{kh}_Nd_N$ and $b=\eta\kappa^h_Mh^{-1}(\kappa^k_N)$ as $c_\bullet\theta_{kh}^\Delta\Delta(d_P)\Delta[Q]^{-1}$ and $u_{h,C_k}h^{-1}(\theta_k^\Delta)\Delta[Q]^{-1}$. Both formulas retain exactly the same inverted resolution map.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: compatibility with composition of the integral identifications

proof.text: The finite units of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] and the termwise compositor of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identify the two strict maps preceding $\Delta[Q]^{-1}$: on local sections, $c_m\theta_{kh,m}d_P(x)=\bar x\otimes1\otimes1=u_{h,C_{k,m}}h^{-1}(\theta_{k,m})(x)$. Tensor balancing uses the coefficient identity of step 1. These are sheafified tensor-unit maps, so the section formulas determine the sheaf maps and commute with differentials. Reducing the same $P$ from $m+1$ to $m$ sends both formulas to $\bar x\otimes1\otimes1$, hence the equality is of strict tower maps. Consequently $\epsilon_D\Delta(a)=\epsilon_D\Delta(b)$.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: compatibility with composition of the integral identifications

proof.text: The bijection $\Phi_{X,D}:f\mapsto\epsilon_D\circ\Delta(f)$ of [lem-trf-integral-comparison-counit-characterization] is injective. Apply it to the equality in step 3 to get $a=b$; cancel the isomorphism $\eta$. This gives precisely $c^E_{h,k,N}\kappa^{kh}_Nd_{h,k,N}=\kappa^h_{Lk^*N}h^{-1}(\kappa^k_N)$ in the ambient completed-coefficient derived category.
